# Performance on the TPU v4-32 slice (generated by `benchmarks/tpu/make_performance_doc.py`)

## Setup

* 16 × TPU v4 (4 hosts × 4 chips), 30.7 GiB HBM per chip; JAX 0.6.2, libtpu 0.0.17, Python 3.10.12 (`runs/env.json`, `scripts/tpu/env_check.py`).
* Model and batch of the confirmatory runs: 123.6M parameters, 240 × 1024 tokens per step, bfloat16 compute, float32 master weights and optimizer state (`configs/base_125m.yaml`).
* One mesh axis over all 16 chips: the batch is sharded, parameters are replicated, and the optimizer state of each bucket of same-shaped matrices (48 × 768×768 and 36 → 48 padded × 768×2048) is sharded along the bucket axis (ZeRO-1). Gradients are reduced in float32; parameter increments are all-gathered (`src/gimbal/jax/distributed.py`).
* Every optimizer gets the same layout, batching, sharding and precision policy: all optimizer matrix products at `Precision.HIGHEST` (float32).

## Attention (gradient step of the full model, median of 20 calls)

| implementation | tiles (q, k, batch) | seconds |
|---|---|---|
| xla | 0, 0, 1 | 0.2083 |
| flash | 0, 0, 1 | 0.2588 |
| flash | 256, 256, 1 | 0.1905 |
| flash | 512, 512, 1 | 0.1701 |
| flash | 1024, 512, 1 | 0.1723 |
| flash | 1024, 1024, 1 | 0.1699 |
| flash | 512, 512, 3 | 0.1699 |
| flash | 1024, 1024, 3 | fails (VMEM) |

Splash attention needs a head dimension that is a multiple of 128 (the model has 64). The Pallas flash-attention kernel with 512 × 512 tiles is used for all runs.

## Gradient step: layers and attention (seconds, median of 20 calls)

| layers, attention | forward | forward + backward (local) |
|---|---|---|
| scan, flash | 0.0407 | 0.1542 |
| scan, xla | 0.0409 | 0.1918 |
| unrolled, flash | 0.0400 | 0.1318 |
| unrolled, xla | 0.0405 | 0.1405 |

With the float32 gradient reduction the step takes 0.1697 s (scan layers); bfloat16 logits would save 0.0023 s and are not used; the output head and loss cost 0.0201 s. Unrolled layers with flash attention are used for all runs.

## Collectives on a 48 × 768 × 2048 array (seconds, median)

| collective | float32 | bfloat16 | HLO op |
|---|---|---|---|
| psum | 0.0083 | 0.0043 | all-reduce |
| psum_scatter_tiled | 0.0083 | 0.0043 | all-reduce |
| psum_scatter_untiled | 0.0083 | 0.0043 | all-reduce |
| all_gather | 0.0077 | 0.0040 | all-gather |

On this runtime XLA lowers a reduce-scatter to an all-reduce of the same cost. Gathering bfloat16 instead of float32 would halve the parameter all-gather for every optimizer alike; it is not used.

## Steady-state step time (gate G4.2)

Definition fixed before measurement (C-017): median over the 20-step blocks of steps 200–400 of the mean step time within a block, from 400-step runs at the confirmatory configuration with real data (`scripts/tpu/time_variants.sh`, `benchmarks/tpu/step_times.py`, logs in `runs/timing/`).

| run | optimizer settings | steady state (ms) | vs SOAP | median of single steps (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| adamw |  | 162.02 | -3.0% | 162.02 |
| soap |  | 166.96 | +0.0% | 164.57 |
| gimbal_k4_a02 | α = 0.02, frame_every = 4, fixed | 170.24 | +2.0% | 165.20 |
| gimbal_k4_a05 | α = 0.05, frame_every = 4, fixed | 170.17 | +1.9% | 165.16 |
| gimbal_adapt_a05 | α = 0.05, frame_every = 4, adaptive | 170.18 | +1.9% | 165.18 |
| gimbal_k2_a05 | α = 0.05, frame_every = 2, fixed | 175.25 | +5.0% | 175.25 |
| gimbal_k1_a05 | α = 0.05, frame_every = 1, fixed | 185.34 | +11.0% | 185.31 |

G4.2 for the default since C-018 (`gimbal_adapt_a05`): 170.18 ms vs SOAP 166.96 ms, fails (+1.9%). The gap is the frame move: on the 2048-dimensional side the retraction, the Newton–Schulz polish and the orthogonality check are float32 products at full precision, which the TPU executes at a fraction of its bfloat16 rate, and the polish needs 3–4 iterations per move because the per-move rotation of a 2048-dimensional frame is large in spectral norm. Phase 04's repair order was followed (batching, amortized retraction); lower-precision rotations would shrink SOAP's and Gimbal's costs alike and cannot close the gap (estimated 0.2 ms). The result is reported as a wall-clock loss.

## Optimizer update cost and its floating-point model (gate G4.3)

Device time per call of each compiled update, from 20-step traces (`benchmarks/tpu/profile_step.py`, minimal trace reader `benchmarks/tpu/xplane.py`); every update includes the all-gather of the parameter increments (≈12.6 ms, identical for all optimizers).

* adamw: gradient step 146.63 ms per step; update modules 15.51 ms, 0.00 ms per step (amortized over the 20 traced steps).
* soap: gradient step 147.06 ms per step; update modules 16.10 ms, 4.18 ms per step (amortized over the 20 traced steps).
* gimbal: gradient step 146.69 ms per step; update modules 14.12 ms, 9.66 ms per step (amortized over the 20 traced steps).

Floating-point model at full-precision float32 (≈37 TFLOP/s measured for the batched 2048³ products):

| work | multiply-adds per device | lower bound (ms) |
|---|---|---|
| SOAP plain step | 4.8e+10 | 2.6 |
| Gimbal plain step | 4.8e+10 | 2.6 |
| Gimbal frame move (extra, 3.5 polish iterations) | 3.46e+11 | 18.7 |

Measured optimizer work beyond the common all-gather stays within 2× of these bounds for SOAP's and Gimbal's matrix products. SOAP's QR refresh is Householder QR (XLA custom calls), which is not bound by matrix-multiply throughput; AdamW's update is memory-bound on the replicated parameters.
